There are a few notable works with very similar titles, so **“Whutcha Want?”** could refer to different things. The exact spelling **“Whutcha Want?”** most strongly points to the **1995 hip-hop single by Nine**.

## 1. “Whutcha Want?” by Nine
- **Artist:** Nine  
- **Released:** 1995  
- **Album:** *Nine Livez*  
- **Genre:** East Coast hip hop  
- **Producer:** Rob Lewis / Tony Stoute-associated production circle is often mentioned around Nine’s work, though credits can vary by source.

### What it is
This was **Nine’s breakout hit** and is by far the best-known work with that exact title spelling. It’s remembered for:
- Nine’s **very deep, gravelly voice**
- a **hard, stripped-down 1990s East Coast sound**
- a repetitive, catchy hook that made it a recognizable rap single of the mid-90s

### Cultural context
Nine emerged during the era when New York rap was packed with rugged, street-oriented artists. “Whutcha Want?” fit into that moment well:
- boom-bap production
- aggressive delivery
- straightforward battle/street energy

It got substantial play on urban radio and on video shows, and it helped establish Nine as more than just a one-off underground figure.

### Charting / impact
It is generally considered Nine’s signature song and biggest hit. Depending on the chart source:
- it charted on **Billboard’s rap-related charts**
- it gained enough visibility to make Nine a recognizable name in 1995

Even if people don’t remember Nine immediately, many rap fans remember the track once they hear it.

### Legacy
“Whutcha Want?” is often brought up in conversations about:
- overlooked 90s rap hits
- one-hit-wonder discussions in hip hop
- distinctive rap voices

Nine followed it with other material, but this remained the song he was most associated with.

---

## 2. Possible confusion: “So Whatcha Want” by Beastie Boys
A lot of people mean this when asking about a similarly titled song.

- **Title:** “So Whatcha Want”  
- **Artist:** Beastie Boys  
- **Released:** 1992  
- **Album:** *Check Your Head*

### Why it gets confused
- Similar phrase
- Much more famous internationally
- Sometimes people remember the title imprecisely

### Key facts
- It’s one of the Beastie Boys’ most iconic tracks
- Known for its dusty, heavy groove and defiant attitude
- The music video, directed by Adam Yauch, is also well known
- A major single in the group’s early-90s reinvention era

---

## 3. Other similarly titled works
There are also other songs named **“Whatcha Want,” “What U Want,”** or close variants by other artists. If you meant a different one, it could be:
- a rap or R&B song
- a TV episode
- a less prominent single with alternate spelling
